String: You feel something nibble on your bait and think it might be enticed to bite if you jerked your rod around.
Something just brushed up against your lure, and you wonder if you should reel it in a little.
The water around your lure keeps moving, as if something is deciding whether or not it wants to bite. You're thinking it might be better to be patient and wait.
You suddenly notice the tip of your pole is <jiggling/wiggling/gently bouncing>, but just a tiny bit.
You don't feel anything while holding your rod but notice the bobber on your bait is bouncing.
You see your float start bobbing on the water but not sure if it's just the wind or if something is nibbling.
You're enjoying the view of the water when suddenly the tip of your rod bends sharply.
You notice the line on your rod is tightening but the tip isn't moving.
As you're slowly reeling in your lure, you think you feel something biting but not sure.
You feel like nothing is biting today, and about to call it quits when you feel a sudden strike as your rod bends hard.
You've been getting some good strikes on your lure but unable to reel anything in, when suddenly you get another strike.
For a second time, you feel something teasing your lure but hesitant to jerk your rod prematurely, as it might get away again.
A couple of fish have already gotten away today, and you're starting to think it's because you're <waiting too long to jerk your rod/jerking your rod prematurely>.
You noticed something nibbling on your lure earlier and tried <reeling it in/jerking your rod> but it got away, now you're feeling another nibble.
You've lost a couple of fish trying to reel them in too quickly when suddenly you feel another strike on the lure.
You notice another fisherman lost a fish by waiting too long to reel it in when suddenly you feel a strike on your line.
You notice the float on your lure is moving but not sure if it's just the water current or a fish.
You overhear another fisherman saying how the hook needs time to set with these fish when suddenly you feel a slight tug and see the tip of your rod bending.
You've heard the trick to catching these fish is to not act too quickly or too slowly when you feel a nibble, when suddenly you feel a slight tug on your line.
You've been jerking your rod at every little nibble but have yet to catch one fish when suddenly you feel another nibble.
